chunk-001:c004.proposition: Information, mental states, functional disorders, and placebo effects make causal interaction between an immaterial mind and a material brain conceptually plausible.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Calling consciousness an illusion is self-undermining because asserting and evaluating the claim already presupposes conscious activity.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Neural correlations establish a mind-brain connection, but the claim that brains create thoughts imports a materialist worldview rather than reporting a scientific finding.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: Emergent physicalism preserves mind-brain integration but does not explain how qualitative first-person consciousness emerges from physical brain structures.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: Panpsychism rightly makes consciousness primary and is compatible with theism, but it leaves unanswered the further question of where fundamental conscious reality originates.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: Even a complete science of consciousness would not explain why consciousness exists fundamentally, whereas theism grounds human consciousness in an eternal conscious God.

chunk-003:chunk-003-c04.proposition: Panpsychism retains an unresolved combination or emergence problem concerning how simpler forms of experience produce complex unified consciousness.

chunk-003:chunk-003-c08.proposition: Conditional on God's existence, divine consciousness supplies a simple explanation of human consciousness without contradicting scientific accounts.
